clue.text: Table's partly laid, and fight's about to start

definitions.meaning: a table with the cutlery set out but not yet the plates is part-laid
the idiom for open hostility being imminent, blades drawn

explanation.surface: A host halfway through setting the table senses a quarrel brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes cutlery set out and idiomatically means people are ready to attack one another.

clue.text: Pitched battle in space?

parts.note: read 'pitched' as on a sports pitch, and 'space' as a patch of territory: a fight over one's ground

explanation.surface: A science-fiction clash between starships.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight over territory or ground, where turf is the grassy pitch and also one's patch.

clue.text: It warms the Cockney consumer

indicators.note: Cockney speech drops the initial H, so the word loses that letter

parts.note: a device that warms a room is a heater

explanation.surface: A London radiator described in dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Cockney' signals the dropped H, as Londoners of the East End famously drop their aitches, leaving EATER.
explanation.definitionFit: One who eats is a consumer of food, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Soap character that's just up one's street

definitions.meaning: A long-running Australian TV soap opera, popular in Britain, so any character in it is one of the title
taken literally, someone living a little further along your road

explanation.surface: A TV soap figure who happens to suit one perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just up one's street' looks like the idiom for something that suits you; read literally it is someone living nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A person living close by on the same street, and also a member of the cast of the soap Neighbours.

clue.text: Striking that I'd missed a test, having no paper

indicators.note: missed says that the letters of I'd are left out of the word before

parts.note: a vivid colour is striking
I'd is written as its letters

explanation.surface: Someone startled to find they skipped an exam with no written part.
explanation.definitionFit: A viva is an oral examination, a test conducted by speaking rather than on paper.

clue.text: Son takes teacher something for tea

parts.note: a trainer teaches skills

explanation.surface: A boy's tutor brings a gift for afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A strainer catches loose leaves when pouring tea, a piece of tea equipment.

clue.text: Optimistic-sounding girl

indicators.note: sounding says the word is identified by how it is pronounced, not its spelling

parts.note: a rosy outlook is optimistic

explanation.surface: A cheerful-seeming young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosie is a girl's name, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Suggest politician takes part of church service

parts.note: to offer is to suggest or propose
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A proposal that a politician joins in a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: The offertory is the section of a Christian service where gifts and the collection are brought forward.

clue.text: I've suddenly realised computer people are over there

definitions.meaning: pointing out the IT department, computer people being IT (information technology)

explanation.surface: Someone has a eureka moment about where the computer staff sit.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation of a breakthrough, and literally a phrase pointing to the IT staff.

clue.text: Pet making a complete recovery?

definitions.meaning: a domestic dog breed kept as a pet
whimsically, one that recovers or fetches back what was shot

explanation.surface: An animal that has fully recuperated from illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A retriever is a gun-dog breed kept as a pet, and literally something that recovers or fetches things.

clue.text: Capital needed in very short order

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: short says the word for order loses its last letter

parts.note: a fiat is an authoritative order or decree

explanation.surface: Money required immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money, and 'short order' like speed; FIAT cut short gives FIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Your job at first is restricted but valuable

indicators.note: at first says the job word comes first, before the word for your
restricted says the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: work is a job
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: A worker's role is limited but still worth something.
explanation.definitionFit: Worthy means having worth or merit, so it is close in sense to valuable.

clue.text: Grabbing new attention, attacks culture

indicators.note: grabbing says the word for attacks holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: fits are sudden attacks of illness or temper
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: Fresh notice provokes outbursts against the arts world.
explanation.definitionFit: Painting, sculpture and music are the fine arts, the core of high culture.

clue.text: Recover from crash, as back of car hits middle of tree

indicators.note: middle of says take the central letters of the word tree

parts.note: the boot is the British word for the luggage space at the back of a car

explanation.surface: A car accident in which the rear of the car strikes a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR added a stray 'pt'; the page has none. 'Crash' looks like a road accident but it is a computer crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Restarting a computer after it has frozen is how one recovers from a crash.

clue.text: Here one serves port to an uncouth type

parts.note: a bar is where drinks are served
Bari is a port in southern Italy

explanation.surface: A bartender serving port wine to a boor.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbarian is a rough, uncivilised person, a synonym for an uncouth type.

clue.text: Drop not put away

definitions.meaning: to drop someone from a team is to omit them
leaving something out rather than tidying it away

explanation.surface: A tidying instruction about what to keep visible.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit is to drop, and an item left on the side has not been put away.

clue.text: All sorts one used to find in a palace?

definitions.text: one used to find in a palace?
definitions.meaning: music-hall theatres in Britain were often called Palace of ..., staging variety shows

explanation.surface: Every kind of thing once found in a royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'palace' suggests royalty; it is the old music-hall theatre called a Palace of Varieties.
explanation.definitionFit: Varieties are different kinds, and variety shows were the staple of the old music-hall Palaces.

clue.text: Deny a mild cold is disastrous

indicators.note: disastrous says the letters are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Insisting a slight chill is no catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is disastrous' rearranges A MILD, C and IS to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclaim is to deny responsibility for or connection with something.

clue.text: One picture or others put back in hole

annotationWithheld.why: One picture or others put back in hole (8): PIT around OR plus TRA, but no sense of 'others' gives ART reversed, so the parse cannot be shown honestly.
annotationWithheld.clue: One picture or others put back in hole

clue.text: Do a good job for each group of children

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: Doing well for every class of pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform well is to do a good job; perform alone carries the sense of doing one's job effectively.

clue.text: Burrowing in bottom of river, fish made nasty noise

indicators.note: burrowing in says the fish goes inside the river bottom

parts.note: a river bed is its bottom
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A fish digging into the riverbed makes an unpleasant sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey brays, a harsh unpleasant cry, so brayed means made a nasty noise.

clue.text: Industrial city is finished — tut-tut!

parts.note: done means finished
tsk is the written sound of disapproval

explanation.surface: Dismay that a manufacturing city is in decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Donetsk is a coal and steel city in eastern Ukraine, an example of an industrial city.

clue.text: Teach rat to move stick back

indicators.note: to move says the letters of the two words shift position

explanation.surface: Training a rodent to shift a stick backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To reattach is to fasten again, to stick something back on.

clue.text: Restricting elements of party in government

indicators.note: elements of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some members of the ruling party hold things back.
explanation.definitionFit: Tying something limits its movement, so tying means restricting.

clue.text: Woman with veg cooking?

parts.note: beet is a vegetable
food that is on is cooking

explanation.surface: A lady preparing vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Isabella Beeton wrote the famous Victorian Book of Household Management, the classic British cookbook.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Beeton was a woman, famous as a Victorian cookery writer.

clue.text: Wall piece stuffed with old cloth

indicators.note: stuffed with says the first word has the other letter put inside

parts.note: a tile is one piece of a wall covering

explanation.surface: Part of a wall padded with aged fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Toile is a linen or cotton fabric, a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Venerable figure's admission of being trickster?

parts.note: saying I am is admitting to being, so I
a con is a trick or a con man

explanation.surface: A revered person confessing to fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: Read together, I CON is the confession of a trickster.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a revered figure, or literally a venerated holy image.

clue.text: Creature I pen backwards

indicators.note: backwards says the letters of the two pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: a Biro is the British brand name for a ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: An author writing in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: The oribi is a small African antelope, an example of a creature.

clue.text: Library worker given new chair with limited view

indicators.note: new says the letters of chair are given fresh order
limited says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a vista is a view

explanation.surface: A librarian gets a new seat but a poor outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns CHAIR into ARCHI; 'limited' cuts VISTA to VIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An archivist keeps records and documents, working in a library or archive.

clue.text: Handling darts at last, top or bull?

parts.note: management is the handling of affairs

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of darts

parts.note: the peak is the top

explanation.surface: A darts match ends in a top score or a bullseye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bull' looks like the darts bullseye; it means nonsense, bull for bullshit.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporate jargon is often dismissed as meaningless nonsense, or bull.
